title: Client Fidelity Intervention Lab
content:
Purpose and use
This is a working lab for high-touch and strategic accounts where we suspect renewal instability. Use as a checklist + playbook for CSMs preparing QBRs, renewal negotiations, or rapid intervention sprints. This document is intentionally modular so teams can borrow snippets (email templates, escalation triggers, remediation tasks) and adapt them to account context.

One‑page assessment (10‑minute routine)
- Quick score (0–100): weighted composite of 5 signals. Compute during prep and update weekly during active saves.
  - Adoption & usage (35%): product MAU/DAU vs baseline; 100 = steady growth, 0 = flatline or fall >70%.
  - Financial cadence (25%): ARR run-rate trend, billing disputes, prep to churn for next invoice.
  - Support friction (15%): sev1 incidents, repeat bugs, unresolved tickets >14d.
  - Strategic alignment (15%): roadmap fit, exec sponsorship, active POCs.
  - Sentiment & engagement (10%): NPS/qualitative cues from champions.
- Example: usage 60, finance 40, support 80, alignment 30, sentiment 50 => score = 60*0.35 + 40*0.25 + 80*0.15 + 30*0.15 + 50*0.10 = 46.5 (High risk).

Risk buckets and thresholds
- Green (70–100): monitor, QBR prep as normal.
- Yellow (50–69): proactive engagement; schedule 2-week tactical check-ins; assign play queue owner.
- Red (<50): trigger intervention. Escalation required if score <50 OR any of the following triggers: churn language from champion, billing hold placed, two or more Sev1 incidents in 60 days, executive sponsor disengaged for >30 days.

Escalation ladder (fast path)
- Triage (CSM): 24h — assemble incident brief, list top 3 root causes, immediate low-effort remediation tasks.
- Manager (CS Team Lead): 48h — approve commercial concessions, orchestrate cross-functional resources.
- Solutions Eng / Product Lead: 72h — technical remediation plan, rollback or hotfix if needed.
- Head of CS / Customer Execs: 5 business days — executive outreach, prepare exec-brief QBR slot, negotiate renewal terms.

30/60/90 day intervention plan templates
- Day 0–7 (Containment)
  - Confirm financial standing (billing, PO status), pause automated renewal notices if needed.
  - Deploy usage audit report and top 5 usage anomalies.
  - Quick wins: targeted training, short-term overrides (rate limits, quota increases), temporary priority support.
  - Communication: CSM email + exec Slack ping; set weekly check-in cadence.
- Day 8–30 (Stabilize)
  - Deliver remediation roadmap with owners and ETA for each item.
  - Run a product health sweep with SE and SRE: confirm incident closure and monitoring hooks.
  - Offer outcome‑aligned concessions (credits, trial extension, feature-enabled pilot) tied to measurable goals.
  - Prepare a tailored QBR deck focused on business outcomes and roadmap alignment.
- Day 31–90 (Recover & Solidify)
  - Execute remediation, demos of fixes, and joint success milestones for customer stakeholders.
  - Launch a 3‑month adoption plan with KPIs and review cadence; automate reporting into their execs.
  - Confirm renewal commitment or plan for staged renewal with checkpoints.

Commercial play options (prescriptive, pick 1–2)
- Short-term credit + SLA uplift for 3 months (for product reliability issues).
- Usage‑based rebate: apply X% rebate if usage stays within agreed bands during the next billing cycle.
- Pilot upgrade path: free access to dedicated capacity for a prioritized POC for 60 days.
- Contract amendments: staged renewal (6 months + option to convert to 12m) for accounts with procurement constraints.

Guided templates: customer-facing email (initial triage)
Subject: Quick follow-up + stabilization plan for [Account Name]
Hi [Champion],
Thanks for the time today — we heard your concern around [primary issue]. We’ve opened a short stabilization plan and here are the immediate items: 1) we’re assigning priority support and a SE to reproduce and patch by EOD, 2) we’ll pause the automated renewal notice while we work this out, 3) proposed check-in cadence: twice weekly for 2 weeks.
We want to be pragmatic about next steps — would you be available on [two time options]?
Best,
[CSM Name]

Template: exec outreach (if escalation to execs)
Subject: Exec sync request — risk mitigation for [Account Name]
Hi [Exec Name],
We’re seeing a drop in platform adoption and billing friction at [Account]. We recommend a 30‑day remediation sprint; early ask is for a 20 minute sync to align on top commercial levers (credits, pilot access, or staged renewal). Attached: one-page risk snapshot and 30/60/90 plan.

Internal playbook checklist (CSM) — tickbox style\- [ ] One‑page risk score completed\- [ ] Usage report attached\- [ ] Billing/PO status verified with Finance\- [ ] Required SE engagement scheduled\- [ ] Draft QBR deck with outcomes slide created\- [ ] Proposed commercial play selected and approved by manager\- [ ] Slack channel for cross‑functional coordination created\- [ ] Exec brief slide (if required) prepared

Sample exec brief slide bullets (1 slide)\- Title: Renewal at Risk — [Account Name] (Score: 43)\- Top issues: 1) sustained 45% drop in key feature usage, 2) procurement delaying PO by 30+ days, 3) two Sev1 incidents in last 8 weeks\- Immediate asks: approve 30% credit as a gesture + pilot on dedicated capacity for 60 days; headcount: SE (0.3 FTE), SRE (on-call), CSM (0.2 FTE)\- Expected outcome: recover to 75% of baseline utilization by day 60; convert to 12m renewal at day 90 if KPIs met

Monitoring and success metrics to track during save sprint\- Weekly score (same rubric)\- Product key metric(s) (MAU, tokens/day, query success rate)\- Time to first response and resolution for open tickets\- Exec engagement logs (last meeting, next scheduled)\- Commercial progress (PO received, credit issued, amendment signed)

Decision matrix: when to stop saving and invoke exit path
- Continue save: if score improves >=12 points in first 30 days and at least one strategic stakeholder re‑engages.
- Change approach to staged renewal: if progress is partial but procurement constraints remain unresolved; offer six‑month stepdown.
- Execute exit: if no meaningful uplift after 60 days AND customer refuses commercial remediation, prepare termination checklist and lock in transition assistance terms.

Legal and compliance checklist (quick hits)
- Confirm contract obligations (SLA language, termination notice windows).
- Validate data handling for any on‑prem/dedicated offers (SOWs, DPA updates).
- Escalate to legal for non‑standard concession > 20% ARR.

CSM play scripts (short)
- On discovery call: "I want to make sure we remove blockers quickly — here are three things we can do this week to keep your team productive."
- For procurement stalls: "We can stage the renewal so you can get immediate cost predictability while procurement completes the PO."
- For feature fit concerns: "Let's scope a 6‑week pilot with measurable KPIs — if we don't hit them, we'll accept the learnings and adjust commercial terms."

Handoff and post‑mortem
- If retention achieved: schedule 30/60/90 day follow-ups and capture lessons learned in the account playbook.\- If churn occurs: complete churn packet (reasons, timeline, what we tried, cost of concessions) and create a root cause summary to share with Product and Eng.

Notes and redlines for CS leadership
- Keep interventions data‑driven: ask Finance and Observability for automated exports to avoid manual errors.
- Limit deep discounts as last resort: prefer product fixes, pilot access or SLA commitments first.
- Train SEs on fast triage flows for top 10 customers by ARR.

Appendix: quick formulas and references\- At‑risk ARR approximation = current ARR * (1 - score/100). Use this as a quick sense-check for expected impact.\- Recommended Slack alert: channel #cs-risk with a bot that posts when an account score drops by >10 points in 7 days.

This doc is a draft lab intended to be iterated. Use the linked artifacts for templates and paste snippets into customer emails — keep a copy of final QBR decks for our knowledge base.
